planting.note: Set out divisions or nursery starts after last frost into well-drained, neutral to alkaline soil; shear lightly after each bloom flush to keep flowers coming.

directions: Grow in lean, sharply drained, neutral to alkaline soil in full sun, since heavy or acidic ground shortens the plant's lifespan. Pink Mist produces a dense mound of ferny gray-green foliage topped by soft dusty-pink pincushion blooms held on wiry stems from late spring into fall, holding its compact, tidy habit better than the species. Deadheading spent flower heads every week or two keeps new buds forming continuously through the heat of summer. Divide congested clumps every two to three years in early spring to maintain vigor and flower count.

planting.note: Plant divisions or transplants around last frost into alkaline, well-drained soil; stake in windy sites since the flower stems are tall and slender.

directions: Site in fertile, alkaline to neutral, well-drained soil in full sun, as acid or waterlogged ground causes rapid decline. Fama is a florist-grade selection prized for its large, clear lavender-blue flower heads on extra-long, sturdy stems that hold up exceptionally well in cutting gardens and floral arrangements. Deadhead continuously through the season to prolong bloom from midsummer to frost, and divide every three to four years to renew vigor. Winter mulch is rarely needed in its hardiness range, but sharp drainage is essential to prevent crown rot.

planting.note: Start seed indoors 6-8 weeks before last frost, since this open-pollinated strain shows some variation in flower shade from packet to packet.

directions: Grow in alkaline to neutral, well-drained, moderately fertile soil in full sun. House's Hybrids is a classic seed-raised strain that yields a broad color range of lavender, violet-blue, and near-white pincushion blooms on long, wiry stems, making it a traditional cutting-garden mainstay grown from open-pollinated seed rather than a single clonal selection. Deadhead regularly to keep new buds forming from midsummer through fall, and expect some plant-to-plant variation in flower tone and size since it is a seed strain rather than a uniform cultivar. Divide the best-performing individual plants after a few seasons to preserve favored color forms.

planting.note: Plant divisions around last frost into alkaline, well-drained soil in full sun; this heirloom selection has been propagated by division since the early 20th century.

directions: Plant in fertile, alkaline to neutral, sharply drained soil in full sun, since this old cultivar declines quickly in acidic or heavy wet ground. Clive Greaves is one of the oldest named Scabiosa caucasica selections still in commerce, valued for its medium lavender-blue, frilled pincushion flowers on tall, gracefully arching stems that have made it a staple cut flower for over a century. Deadhead through the season to sustain bloom from midsummer into fall, and divide clumps every three to four years since the cultivar loses vigor in congested crowns. Good air circulation helps prevent powdery mildew in humid climates.

planting.note: Set out nursery starts or divisions after last frost into well-drained soil; shear spent flowering stems to encourage rebloom.

directions: Grow in well-drained, neutral to slightly alkaline soil in full sun for the deepest flower color. Vivid Violet is a compact hybrid selection bred for saturated violet-purple pincushion blooms held above tidy, ferny foliage, offering richer color than many older lavender-blue selections. Deadhead every one to two weeks through summer to keep the long bloom cycle going from late spring to frost, and divide congested clumps every two to three years to maintain flower quality. It performs best where summer nights stay relatively cool, showing reduced rebloom in hot, humid climates.

planting.note: Direct sow in early spring or start indoors 6-8 weeks before last frost; Mars Midget stays compact enough for the front of the border or a container.

directions: Sow into well-drained, alkaline to neutral soil in full sun. Mars Midget is a dwarf selection of crimson scabious bred to stay under 18 inches tall, roughly half the height of the species, while still producing the same abundance of deep wine-red pincushion flowers from June through frost. Its compact habit resists flopping without staking, making it well suited to border edges, rock gardens, and containers where the taller species would sprawl. Deadhead regularly to prolong bloom and curb excessive self-seeding, since the species and its dwarf forms readily naturalize in favorable conditions.

planting.note: Direct sow in early spring or start indoors 6-8 weeks before last frost; this seed strain shows a full range of pastel tones from packet-raised plants.

directions: Sow into well-drained, alkaline to neutral soil in full sun. Melton Pastels is an open-pollinated seed strain that departs from the species' typical deep crimson, instead producing a soft mix of pink, salmon, lavender, cream, and dusky red pincushion flowers on the same wiry, branching stems from June through frost. Because it is seed-grown rather than a single clone, expect some variation in exact shade between individual plants. Deadhead to extend bloom and limit self-seeding, and consider selecting and dividing your favorite color forms to keep them true from year to year.

common_name: Thunder and Lightning Variegated Crimson Scabious

planting.note: Propagate by division to preserve the variegation, since seedlings often revert to plain green foliage; plant after last frost into well-drained soil.

directions: Plant divisions in well-drained, alkaline to neutral soil in full sun to light shade, since some afternoon shade helps preserve the leaf variegation in hot climates. Thunder and Lightning is a striking foliage sport of crimson scabious with cream-and-green splashed leaves that provide season-long interest even before the deep wine-red pincushion flowers appear from June through frost. Remove any all-green reverted shoots promptly at the base to keep the clump variegated, and divide every two to three years to maintain both vigor and leaf pattern. Because named divisions are the only reliable way to keep the variegation true, source new plants vegetatively rather than from seed.
